text:
maya_support: Hey team, NimbusProd (customer=nimbus) started seeing recurring 429s at the top of every minute for the last 3 hours. Ticket attached: #INC-4829. Sample client log: 

nimbus-client - 2026-03-17T09:00:01Z - POST /v1/generate - 429 Too Many Requests - x-request-id=abc123
Headers returned: X-RateLimit-Limit: 120/min, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, Retry-After: 30

They claim they haven't changed code. Not sure if it's a client retry loop or a scheduled job. Can SRE help verify server-side throttling and whether it's hitting our RPM/TPM caps?

liam_sre: Looking now. Ran quick query against request logs for customer:nimbus grouped by minute — yep, sharp spikes at :00, :01 then tailing off. Peaks ~140 requests/min which exceeds their 120/min RPM. We also see a second series of short-lived connections from an IP pool (10.7.x.x) at the same times.

maya_support: Thanks. Any header details from our side (we add X-RateLimit-* in responses)?

rate-limit-bot: Automated alert - customer "nimbus" hit per-customer RPM cap at 2026-03-17T09:00:01Z. Policy: standard-tier (120 RPM / 6000 TPM). Backoff suggested: exponential with jitter.

toni_csm: Pinging Nimbus rep to get their view. @nimbus_prod_rep can you confirm if you have any cron/polling jobs scheduled at minute boundaries? Any recent deploys?

nimbus_prod_rep: We rolled out a streaming reconnect change yesterday but all kept same cadence. We do have a heartbeat worker that polls every minute for status updates. We'll check if reconnects are triggering duplicate requests.

alex_engineer: Quick repro you can run from our admin console to simulate: 

curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -X POST --connect-timeout 2 -s -D - | sed -n '1,20p'

Look for X-RateLimit-Remaining and Retry-After. If we see Remaining=0 and 429 body, server-side is correctly rejecting. Also check our internal metric: customer.rate_limit.exceeded.count and customer.req.per_minute.

liam_sre: I've pulled more detailed logs. Two patterns: (1) a burst of short POSTs from same auth key in <200ms windows at :00 leading to remaining=0, then (2) client-side immediate retries without backoff — we see retries at :00:01 and :00:02. That's the retry-loop compounding the spike.

maya_support: So we have a classic burst + aggressive retry loop. Best remediation steps?

liam_sre: Immediate mitigation options: 
- Enable temporary per-customer smoothing: apply token-bucket smoothing policy for nimbus, cap bursts to 4 reqs/sec (we can do this for 1-2 hours).
- Increase their RPM to 200 temporarily if they need higher sustained throughput while they fix client.
- Add server-side 429 with Retry-After and encourage clients to implement exponential backoff + jitter. We already return Retry-After but client ignores it.

toni_csm: I'll ask Nimbus to instrument backoff and add jitter. They may prefer we raise the cap for a short window while they patch. Want to propose: temporary +50% RPM and a scheduled follow-up to ensure throttling behavior improves.

nimbus_prod_rep: We can push a hotfix to the heartbeat worker in 30m to add jitter and stop immediate retries. In the short term, please do the smoothing — their UX is priority.

liam_sre: Done — applied smoothing policy for customer:nimbus (caps: burst_max=8, steady_rate=2r/s). Monitoring now.

rate-limit-bot: Policy change logged: smoothing applied by liam_sre at 2026-03-17T09:10:12Z.

maya_support: After smoothing applied, error rate dropped from ~35% to ~4% in the next 3 minutes. Still seeing occasional 429s at the spikes but much less pronounced.

alex_engineer: For root cause, looks like their streaming reconnect + heartbeat at same minute boundary created duplicated concurrent requests. Recommend they randomize cron and add jitter async. Sample client fix: 

// JS pseudo
setTimeout(()=>{ backoffAndSend() }, Math.random() * 1000)

Also advise exponential backoff: retryDelay = base * 2^attempt + random(0, jitter)

nimbus_prod_rep: Hotfix deployed. We'll monitor for 2 hours and get back. Really appreciate the quick smoothing action.

toni_csm: I'll log follow-up: offer a short-term RPM increase if they need it during migration. Also note: suggest Dedicated or Dedicated burst add-on for predictable throughput if this pattern persists.

maya_support: Marking ticket INC-4829 as "triaged - smoothing applied". Will keep thread open until Nimbus confirms clean. :white_check_mark: 

liam_sre: Adding checklist for post-mortem: client heartbeat jitter, verify client honors Retry-After, consider rate-limit dashboard alert for top 5 customers spiking at minute boundaries.

nimbus_prod_rep: All green so far after hotfix. Thanks everyone.

maya_support: Closing loop in 4 hours if no regression.
